problem_type: Every on-screen video node mounts a fully buffering <video>, while the poster the asset boundary already derives is never drawn
symptom: Mac user, real project with 30+ 15-second 1080p generated video nodes: hovering the canvas lags behind the cursor, dragging and typing feel sticky. Measured on Windows with 32 such nodes in view: every node mounts <video preload="auto" controls> (readyState 4, 12–15 s buffered each) and the GPU process holds 1.3–2.0 GB; the @ candidate list takes 1.1–2.9 s to show thumbnails because it loads originals and extracts a 16-frame filmstrip per video.
direct_cause: BaseGenerationNode renders NodeVideoPlaybackGuard → DeferredNodeVideo with preload="auto" for every video result and never reads result.thumbnailUrl. The media queue (deferredNodeMediaQueue) only limits concurrent loading, so loaded players stay mounted. electron/assets/assetPreview.ts derives a first-frame poster for every stored video (a20bf49ce), but the canvas half that consumed it (3a72f0ce7) was reverted together with an unrelated screen-size LOD change on 2026-09-15 (fae43a80e / 29e232a31) and never came back.
class_root: Two owners of one fact drifted apart: the asset boundary decided "the canvas draws a poster and creates <video> only on interaction", the node card kept "always mount a buffering player". Nothing structural asserted the boundary's promise, so bundling it into a reverted commit removed it silently; bookkeeping (PR #787 merged, TODO T-CV-01 "poster half landed") kept saying it was there. Separately, three surfaces derived video covers three ways (asset preview, timeline filmstrip first cell, raw original).
affected_population: Every user of 0.22.x with video results on the canvas; cost scales with the number of video nodes in view (worst on unified-memory Macs)
Old nodes whose results predate the asset-boundary poster, or entered through the reverted import / relocalize / library-drag paths, have no thumbnailUrl
Not affected: image nodes (already had lazy previews), timeline and preview dialog players (one player each)
entry_points: import adapter / canvas stage drop / asset library drag (result.thumbnailUrl written at creation)
resultMediaBackfillBridge (project open: relocalize remote results, backfill posters for local results)

external_sources.purpose: preload=auto pins roughly 10 s of bitrate (2–50 MB) per element and whole files under 25 MB; metadata stops the pipeline before decoder init. Idle players are reclaimed only after 15 s or beyond 8 idle players (renderer_web_media_player_delegate.cc#43), so 30 buffered players are not bounded by the browser.
Prior art for many videos in one view: thumbnail at rest,

invariants: A canvas video node at rest mounts no <video>; it draws the asset-boundary poster
At most one canvas node video plays at a time; a hover preview never interrupts a video the user is watching
Video covers everywhere come from the asset-boundary preview (one derivation owner)

invariant_owner_layer.why: NodeVideoPlaybackGuard is the only place that decides whether a canvas video has a <video> element (dwell / engaged / focus / user playback / unmeasured probe); nodeVideoPlayback owns how mounted elements play and the single-player claim. Poster derivation stays in electron/assets/assetPreview.ts, reached through ensureLocalAssetPreview for old results.

door_reduction.why_not: Cover derivation had three sources (asset preview, AssetVideoCover filmstrip first cell, raw originals in the @ list); after this change the asset-boundary preview is the only one. The guard is rendered only by BaseGenerationNode; claim / backfill / ensure-preview each have a single writer.

generality_proof: Whether a canvas video has a player is decided in one component for every entry (generated, imported, dragged, relocalized, old projects), and every entry that lacks a poster is healed by one bridge through the one derivation owner, so no card falls back to a permanently buffering player.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Poster at rest; <video> only while hovered (after dwell), primary-selected, focused, user-playing or unmeasured; released on unmount.
Returns (deriving if needed) the asset-boundary preview for a stored nomi-local asset through attachStoredAssetPreview.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: resolveLightweightNodePreview already prefers result.thumbnailUrl; backfilled posters make it draw an image instead of a metadata <video>.
Mounted only while the tray is open on one node; preload=metadata.
One player per clip node, already has a poster; editing surfaces are out of this round.

recurrence.reason: The same drift (boundary promises a poster, card mounts a player) can return from any new entry that creates video results without a thumbnail, or from any revert that bundles unrelated work.
same_class_scan: rg "DeferredNodeVideo|<video" src/workbench/generationCanvas: guard, lightweight card, result stack, clip preview (dispositions above)
rg "thumbnailUrl" writers: import adapter, stage drop, asset library drag, relocalize, task localize — all forward the boundary preview now

prevention.invariant: Idle canvas mounts zero <video>; at most one plays
prevention.failure_mode: Unit tests on the playback policy and backfill; the canvas-follow-hand structural check (idle <video> = 0) runs in CI once the harness lands.
prevention.strategy: Keep the mount decision in the guard and cover derivation in the asset boundary; backfill instead of per-surface fallbacks.

legacy_paths.rationale: The DOM-querying hover hook is replaced by props into the guard; the relocalize bridge became resultMediaBackfillBridge (same owner, now also backfills posters); AssetVideoCover no longer uses the timeline filmstrip as a cover.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency change; Chromium behaviour is used as documented.

migration: No data migration. Old results gain result.thumbnailUrl lazily when a project opens (persisted, no undo entry, no canvas event); nothing is rewritten if derivation fails.
residual_risks: First hover on a video now pays player startup (after a 120 ms dwell); decode-failure healing also starts on first hover instead of at load.
Mac hover latency is attributed to memory pressure by inference; Mac confirmation is pending.
